Not wrong under every reading. Lines 15 to 16 say the remark was 'evidently too much for Captain Brown to take placidly'. Lines 32 to 33 have him screw his lips up and drum on the table. So 'Angrily' has real support, and the new clause 'as he could not keep his temper' nearly paraphrases lines 15 to 16. The execution says 'anger is a likely-sounding manner the lines never give', true only of lines 35 to 37, and leaves out lines 15 to 16 and 32 to 33, which point the other way. Use a manner the passage flatly denies. Or put the needed 'not' on the loud-voice seat: 'In a loud voice that Miss Jenkyns could not miss.'
